voice: Ship AI (the narrator): warm, clear, encouraging mission-control voice; British or Indian English; age 25-35; smiling; never rushed.

lines.text: Welcome, Space Commander! We have a new landing mission.
Our landing site is on that ocean planet.
Use the joystick to turn the ship. Put the planet inside the circle.
Locked on! Now push the thrust lever all the way up.
Wow! A planet covered in water.
Hold the DESCEND button to fly down through the clouds.
We need to find a safe place for it to land.
Let's send the survey drone to check the area.
Click the LAUNCH button to launch the drone.
It is too dark to see the landing zones.
Start the scanner to search the area.
Great! The scanner found five sets of landing zones.
Look! Each set of landing zones has a different shape.
Five spaceships are on their way to this planet, and each one has a different shape.
Each spaceship must land on the zone that matches it perfectly, not too small and not too big.
To find the perfect spot for every spaceship, we need to know the area of these shapes.
So let's learn how to find the area of each shape!
Welcome back, Space Commander! Now you know how to find the area of every shape.
Let's land the spaceships, one by one.
Here comes our first spaceship!
Next, we need to find how much space the spaceship needs.
Its area is side times side.
Calculate the area of the spaceship, and select the land with the required area.
Here comes our second spaceship!
Its area is length times width.
Find the area of the spaceship, and select the suitable land.
Great landings, Commander! Three more spaceships are waiting. Let's bring them down!
Here comes our third spaceship!
Its area is base times height.
Here comes our fourth spaceship!
Its area is half times diagonal 1 times diagonal 2.
Here comes our last spaceship!
Its area is half times the sum of the parallel sides times the height.
Perfect match! The spaceship fits exactly.
Landing successful! Great work, Space Commander.
This landing zone is too small. The spaceship cannot fit safely.
This landing zone is too large. Try to find the exact match.
Choose the landing zone with the exact area.
Out of hearts! Autopilot will land on the zone that fits.
20 is the distance all the way around the ship. Area is the space it covers: side times side.
Work out side times side: 5 times 5.
24 is the distance all the way around the ship. For area, multiply length times width.
Check the width: it is 4 units. Length times width is 8 times 4.
26 is the distance all the way around the ship. Area is base times height.
42 uses the slanted side. Use the height: base times height.
20 is the distance all the way around the ship. Area is half of diagonal 1 times diagonal 2.
Multiply the two diagonals, then take half.
40 uses only the shorter parallel side. Add both parallel sides first.
60 uses only the longer parallel side. Add both parallel sides first.
Here's a hint. Work out 5 times 5.
Here's a hint. Work out 8 times 4.
Here's a hint. Work out 7 times 5.
Here's a hint. Work out half of 6 times 8.
Here's a hint. Add 8 and 12, then multiply by 5, and take half.
All five spaceships have landed safely. Great work, Space Commander!
